title: Controlling charge and spin currents through nonreciprocal dissipative processes
abstract: We investigate the generation and control of both charge and spin currents via nonreciprocal dissipative mechanisms in a two-dimensional spinful fermionic atom quantum system with broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries. Within the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad master equation formalism and using an approach based on the time-dependent generalized Gibbs ensemble, we identify in the weak dissipative coupling regime the minimal set of nonreciprocal jump operators required to induce charge and spin currents and to control both their direction and magnitude. We find that in the presence of finite tunneling, Rashba coupling and magnetic field, the combine application of two jump operators nonreciprocally coupling each spin species to a different spatial direction of motion is sufficient to generate both types of current. Furthermore, by tuning the degree of nonreciprocity of the jump operators we modify the dominant transport mechanism from spin to charge. Finally, we checked that this nonreciprocal current generation mechanism is robust to the application of dephasing noise as even in the presence of this additional dissipative process the steady-state occupation distributions for the quasiparticle modes of the Hamiltonian remains non-trivial, an essential requirement to obtain non-zero currents.
summary: The paper demonstrates a method to control charge and spin currents in fermionic quantum systems by engineering nonreciprocal dissipative couplings. Using the GKSL master equation formalism, the authors show that specific dissipation channels can induce finite currents even when starting from a coherent Hamiltonian. This mechanism is robust against dephasing noise, offering a pathway for current manipulation using engineered open system dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how charge and spin currents can be generated and precisely controlled in a quantum system by utilizing nonreciprocal dissipative processes.
main_result: The combination of specific nonreciprocal jump operators is sufficient to generate both charge and spin currents, and tuning the nonreciprocity allows switching the dominant transport mechanism between spin and charge.
method: The analysis employs the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation formalism within the weakly dissipative coupling regime, utilizing a time-dependent generalized Gibbs ensemble approach to find steady states.
model_or_system: The model is a two-dimensional spinful fermionic atom quantum system on a square lattice. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating kinetic, Rashba SOC, and Zeeman terms, coupled to nonreciprocal dissipative jump operators.
key_observables: Charge current ($J^c$) and Spin current ($J^{\sigma eta}$), derived using U(1) and SU(2) gauge transformations.
important_parameters: Nonreciprocity strength (phases $\phi$), tunneling amplitude ($t$), Rashba coupling ($\alpha$), magnetic field ($h$), and the degree of dephasing noise.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the weak dissipative coupling regime, and approximations are made for small phase variations and small angles during gauge transformations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 sketches the model setup, illustrating coherent tunneling and Rashba coupling alongside the action of two specific nonreciprocal dissipative channels required to induce currents.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first defining the physical model (Hamiltonian and dissipation), then deriving the current operators using gauge transformations, detailing the generalized Gibbs ensemble method for steady states, and finally presenting results on current generation, necessary ingredients, and noise robustness.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics in condensed matter contexts, showing how engineered dissipation can mimic or enhance coherent transport phenomena like spin-charge conversion, which is highly relevant to spintronics and topological materials research.

FIG. 2: Steady-state charge currents in the x-direction, Jx c , and y-direction, Jy c , as a function of the phase ϕ for two ra- tios α/h = {0.5, 4}, no dephasing (Γd = 0) and small ΓNR considering a half-filled system of size L × L = 10 × 10 with periodic boundary conditions. Both spin currents Jx σy and Jy σx have the same value and the direction of both currents can be re- versed by changing ϕ.
